connectors.name: Affinidi Portal
connectors.description: A comprehensive identity and data management platform enabling organizations to issue and verify verifiable credentials with privacy-preserving data sharing.

connectors.name: Auth0 Platform
connectors.description: Auth0's experimental mDL and verifiable credentials platform enabling organizations to issue and verify digital credentials integrated with Auth0's identity platform.

connectors.name: Cleverbase Wallet Connector
connectors.description: Integration platform to request verified attributes from an EUDI wallet and to issue EAA, PubEAA, or QEAA into it.

connectors.name: Credenco Business Wallet (Issuer & Verifier API)
connectors.description: Issuer and verifier modules of the Credenco Business Wallet, exposed through a REST API. Backends start OpenID4VCI issuance from credential templates and create OpenID4VP authorization requests from verifier templates, then poll or receive callbacks for the verified claims.

connectors.name: CredIssuer
connectors.description: CredIssuer is a digital credentialing platform that enables institutions and governments to issue tamper-proof, verifiable certificates in real time.

connectors.name: DALION
connectors.description: An enterprise digital identity platform providing complete issuer, and verifier capabilities for organizational credential management.

connectors.name: DIDroom
connectors.description: An open-source decentralized identity platform providing issuer and verifier capabilities with a focus on privacy and user sovereignty.

connectors.name: Digidentity EUDI Wallet Verifier
connectors.description: API that lets a relying party verify credentials from eIDAS 2.0 EUDI Wallets. The caller names the attributes to verify, receives a QR code and deeplink, and gets the shared attributes back over SAML or OpenID Connect. Digidentity describes the service as the intermediary between the relying party and the wallet holder. The product page lists mDoc, SD-JWT and JWT, and says the API implements the protocols in the EU Architecture Reference Framework.

connectors.name: EUDI Wallet Playground
connectors.description: Sandbox for issuing and verifying EUDI Wallet credentials from one place. Operators create templates, sign credentials and deliver them to a wallet by link or QR, and can revoke them. Verification requests PID, attestations or combined presentations, including in-browser OpenID4VP through the W3C Digital Credentials API. The same page offers SaaS or self-hosted deployment with the operator's own keys, and names mobile documents (mDoc) for citizen and document verification.

connectors.name: EUDIPLO
connectors.description: Open-source middleware that a backend calls to issue and verify EUDI Wallet attestations. It implements OpenID4VCI 1.0 and OpenID4VP 1.0 with DCQL, SD-JWT VC and ISO/IEC 18013-5 mdoc, publishes a Token Status List, and returns the result by webhook, server-sent events or polling. Operators run it themselves as a container, with optional PostgreSQL, S3-compatible storage and an external key store. One instance can serve many tenants. It is an LF Decentralized Trust project, previously hosted by the OpenWallet Foundation.

connectors.name: Gataca Studio
connectors.description: Gataca Studio is a cloud-based digital identity platform enabling organizations to interact with ID wallets. From an intuitive dashboard, companies can manage credential issuance and verification to support simple, private, and compliant identity verification and authentication across digital services. Gataca Studio currently works with the Gataca Wallet and other ID wallets aligned with the EU Digital Identity Wallet and European Business Wallet requirements. Built on open standards, the platform supports multiple trust frameworks and integrates easily with existing systems through open APIs without dependence on a specific infrastructure.
credentialStatusMethods: W3C Verifiable Credentials Status List v2021

connectors.name: Hopae Connect
connectors.description: Sandbox verifier for EUDI Wallet presentations through one REST API. Hopae Connect currently gives customers sandbox access to Germany's d-you wallet and Denmark's AltID wallet. Hopae says that support stays sandbox-only until those wallets are available to businesses in production. OpenID Foundation certification for Hopae Connect covers OpenID4VP 1.0 with HAIP 1.0 for the SD-JWT VC and ISO mdoc verifier profiles.

connectors.name: Identfy Business Wallet
connectors.description: Identfy Business Wallet is an enterprise-grade organizational identity solution designed for managing, issuing and presenting corporate verifiable credentials in B2B and B2G environments. It provides a scalable, production-ready platform for handling business credentials such as licenses, powers of attorney, certificates and registry-based attributes, while enabling secure presentation to third parties with verifiable trust. Integrated through REST APIs and wallet connectors, the solution supports flexible on-premise and cloud deployments and combines HSM-backed operations, role-based access control, encryption and traceability to meet demanding enterprise and public-sector requirements. It is aligned with the European digital identity ecosystem, including EUDI and EU Business Wallet scenarios.

connectors.name: Inji Certifier
connectors.description: An open-source issuing component by MOSIP enabling governments and organizations to issue verifiable credentials at scale.

connectors.name: Inji Verifier
connectors.description: An open-source verification component by MOSIP enabling organizations and relying parties to verify verifiable credentials using OpenID4VP.

connectors.name: Lissi EUDI Wallet Connector
connectors.description: Containerized software component that gives organisations a single API to issue and verify attestations with EUDI Wallets via OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP. For production it is a Docker package that runs in the customer's own environment, including a private cloud, with a separate cloud offering for testing. The same API covers PID identification, SCA, EAA and QEAA attestations, and QES-related flows, and signs with keys in the customer's HSM or key vault. Holds OpenID Foundation conformance certification for OpenID4VCI 1.0 and OpenID4VP 1.0, both with HAIP 1.0, and supports multi-tenant operation and trust management.

connectors.name: MATTR VII
connectors.description: Cloud platform for issuing and verifying ISO mdocs. MATTR VII issues mdocs with OpenID4VCI 1.0, using the authorization-code and pre-authorized-code flows, and verifies remote mdoc presentations with OpenID4VP as profiled by ISO/IEC 18013-7:2025 Annex B. That profile follows OpenID4VP draft 18 rather than the final 1.0 specification, and remote verification requests mdocs only. Each customer uses an isolated tenant on a regional shared cloud or a dedicated cloud. The platform is reached through REST APIs and OAuth clients, and the verifier web SDK starts the browser session.

connectors.name: Orbit Enterprise
connectors.description: An enterprise digital identity platform providing verifier and issuer capabilities for organizations to manage and issue verifiable credentials.

connectors.name: Organisation Wallet Suite (Issuer & Verifier)
connectors.description: Issuer and verifier functions of the iGrant.io Organisation Wallet Suite, available on-premise or as multi-tenant PaaS. Issues credentials with OpenID4VCI 1.0 and verifies them with OpenID4VP 1.0 and DCQL, supporting SD-JWT VC, mdoc and W3C VC (JWT), with webhook notifications and OpenID Foundation HAIP 1.0 conformance testing.

connectors.name: Paradym Platform
connectors.description: An enterprise platform for issuing and verifying verifiable credentials, built on the open-source Credo framework.

connectors.name: Procivis One Core
connectors.description: Open-source core used to issue and verify credentials on infrastructure you run yourself, in your data center or at a cloud provider. It exposes a REST API and server SDKs, issues with OpenID4VCI 1.0, and verifies with OpenID4VP 1.0 and the ISO/IEC 18013-5 proximity flow. Documented credential formats are SD-JWT VC and ISO mdoc. Revocation can use a Token Status List, a Bitstring Status List or a CRL. Licensed under Apache-2.0. Desk, the Business Wallet and the Verifier App are separate enterprise components.

connectors.name: Scytales EU Reference Wallet
connectors.description: An organizational platform based on the EU Digital Identity Wallet reference implementation, providing issuer and verifier capabilities.

connectors.name: Scytáles Wallet Connector
connectors.description: Verifier listed by the OpenID Foundation as Wallet Connector 1.0 from Scytales AB. The certification covers OpenID4VP 1.0 with HAIP 1.0 for SD-JWT VC and ISO mdoc presentations. The public developer portal describes remote and same-device validation with OpenID Connect and the W3C Digital Credentials API.

connectors.name: SICPA Digital Trust Suite
connectors.description: An enterprise digital trust platform from SICPA providing issuer and verifier capabilities for secure credential management, building on their expertise in security authentication.

connectors.name: SnapKYC
connectors.description: SnapKYC is a consent-first business verification platform that enables organizations to verify digital credentials. Supports OID4VP-based presentations including mDL/mDoc, SD-JWT VC and VCDM credentials.

connectors.name: Sphereon Business Wallet
connectors.description:
The Sphereon business wallet is an enterprise-grade, API-first application service that provides the comprehensive functionality required to manage the complete digital credential lifecycle. It enables organizations to seamlessly operate as issuers, holders, and verifiers of verifiable credentials. Designed for ecosystem interoperability, it supports cross-border European standards including eIDAS 2.0 profiles, SD-JWT, and ISO 18013-5 mdocs. Its headless architecture allows it to integrate silently into existing ERP, GRC, and procurement workflows, allowing organizations to automate compliance and trust without forcing employees to adopt new standalone interfaces.

What distinguishes the Sphereon business wallet from standard digital identity applications is its underlying Sphereon Verifiable Data Exchange (VDX) trust engine. While most wallets passively hold or perform basic checks on credentials, the Sphereon wallet actively gates business operations.

This allows organizations to create an authoritative semantic model of their specific operational world. Using integrated industry-standard decision engines, the wallet evaluates every single action and credential exchange against internal organizational policies, external regulations, and technical specifications.

The result is that every data exchange produces a definitive outcome ( Permit, Deny, or Step-Up) that dictates subsequent workflow steps. Furthermore, instead of relying on standard system logs, every decision and its surrounding context is cryptographically written to a tamper-proof, hash-chained audit trail. The Sphereon business wallet does not just verify data; it provides a legally defensible, perfectly reconstructable record of continuous assurance for every operational decision.

connectors.name: Sphereon VDX platform
connectors.description:
Sphereon VDX is a verifiable data layer for policy-driven trust and audit-ready decisions. It is a deployable verifiable data exchange platform that verifies evidence, resolves trust, applies policy, and returns auditable decisions to your existing business systems.

It is an omni-channel enterprise developer platform supporting management of organizational wallets, mobile wallets and identity integrations, providing holder, issuer, and verifier capabilities with DIIP v5, HAIP and OID4VCI/VP 1.0, ISO-18013-5/7 compliance.

Where our open-source Sphereon Identity Development Kit (IDK) provides low-level cryptographic control and our Sphereon Enterprise development Kit (EDK) provides production-grade building blocks, the Sphereon Verifiable data Exchange (VDX) platform provides the deployable verifiable data layer with APIs, management tooling, workflow support, and reusable solution patterns for enterprise operations.

See our developer documentation for all details or contact us for a free consultation

connectors.name: Spherity's European Business Wallet
connectors.description: Spherity’s European Business Wallet (EBW) enables the seamless exchange of verifiable credentials across organisations, from banking, insurance and beyond. As part of the EBW framework and fully eIDAS

connectors.name: SWIYU Generic Issuer
connectors.description: Generic issuer component of the SWIYU ecosystem, enabling organizations to issue verifiable credentials to compatible wallets within the Swiss e-ID infrastructure.

connectors.name: SWIYU Generic Verifier
connectors.description: Generic verifier component of the SWIYU ecosystem, enabling organizations to request and verify verifiable presentations from compatible wallets within the Swiss e-ID infrastructure.

connectors.name: TrustTech ID Connector
connectors.description: ID connector that lets organisations accept certified EUDI Wallets, business wallets, eIDs, bank logins and document reads through one OpenID Connect integration. Returns a normalised result with an assurance level, handles relying-party registration, access certificates, wallet unit attestation checks and revocation checks, and runs as a managed service, in a private cloud or on-premise. The package is containerised and can use an HSM or keystore. EUDI Wallet verification uses OpenID4VP and DCQL, with SD-JWT VC and ISO mdoc under the HAIP profile. The product page lists OpenID4VCI among the same standards.

connectors.name: Truvera Platform
connectors.description: A blockchain-based verifiable credentials platform enabling organizations to issue and verify tamper-proof digital credentials.

connectors.name: Ver.iD Platform
connectors.description: Hosted platform to sign in with a digital identity wallet, request verified data (disclosure) and issue digital credentials. Flows are configured in Ver.iD Studio and run through the Ver.iD Gateway (hosted or embedded), with TypeScript SDKs and OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect integration. Supported wallets include Yivi, Datakeeper, Digidentity and NL Wallet (testing).

connectors.name: Veres Wallet
connectors.description: An enterprise-grade verifiable credentials platform built by Digital Bazaar, pioneers of the W3C Verifiable Credentials standard, offering issuer and verifier capabilities.

connectors.description: VS Agent is the reference implementation of a Verifiable Service: an open-source, self-hosted business wallet that gives every service an organization operates a verifiable identity, so anyone can che

connectors.name: walt.id Community Stack
connectors.description: Open-source issuer and verifier APIs from the walt.id Community Stack. Issuer API v2 issues W3C VC JWTs, SD-JWT VCs and mdocs with OpenID4VCI 1.0. Verifier API v2 checks those formats with OpenID4VP 1.0. The stack also implements HAIP 1.0. You run it yourself, on your own infrastructure or in a private cloud. Portal2 is a white-label UI for issuance and verification. The Issuer and Verifier management APIs do not authenticate callers, so they have to be kept private before production use. This record does not include the separate Wallet API.
